input.summary:
Roofs and chimneys: the four brick stacks now build from y18 up through the roof with their signal fires, plus the rear-porch shed roof (448 placed).
REFUSED 224 -> 0 and OFF-PALETTE none; ./make.sh runs clean and writes build.nbt.
The in-house stack cells (grid y4..17) and the hearths are dropped, since the shell owns them.
left: Stacks inside the house are missing: the shell leaves air at the four stack footprints (x33-34/61-62, z46-47/56-57) from grid y3 to y17, so those cells are locked and this part can't write bricks there. Fix belongs in the shell: keep the stack columns solid (or exclude them from room air) for y0..17.
Stack bricks above the plate (y18 up) now float: nothing under them at y17, so the attic section is an unsupported group until the shell fix lands.

Hearths (fireboxes at y4..5 and y11..12 in each stack face) are not built. They were removed from roofs.mjs because every firebox write is in shell-owned cells; the firebox/hearth code needs to come back once the shell leaves those cells open.

Vocabulary offset, not fixed here (outside the two requested fixes): vocab/h4.mjs chimneyStack assumes grid y = site y + SITE_Y (4), but build.mjs and vocab/base.mjs use grid y = plan y. So chimneyStack(..., {y:0}) writes grid 4..31 instead of 0..27, and the stacks stand 4 cells too high. The one-line workaround is {y: -4} in roofs.mjs, or fix SITE_Y in h4.mjs.
The extra signal campfire at grid y27 (roofs.mjs) sits inside the stack under the chimneyStack flue; the owner of the chimney design should confirm it is wanted.

waste.what: Finding which cells were refused took several steps: the runParts report keeps only the first 8 refused writes (all at y4-5), so I had to re-run with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and tabulate the shell's owned cells by hand to learn the real set (16 columns x 14 rows, grid y4..17).
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one probe script; the 224-count was only explained after reading the lock code in build.mjs
waste.tool: runParts report should list every refused cell grouped by column or y-band (or write them to parts-report.json), not the first 8. A `mcd lock-map <part>` command that prints owned cells per part would show a footprint's conflicts in one table.

waste.what: Discovered that vocab/h4.mjs assumes a grid origin of site y -4 (SITE_Y = 4), contradicting vocab/base.mjs and build.mjs (grid y = plan y). Every helper using SITE_Y puts its stacks 4 cells high; I only found it by comparing the refused coordinates (grid y4) with the plan's y0.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls of reasoning from coordinates; nothing was built wrong beyond this part
waste.tool: A vocab conformance check (`mcd check --vocab`, or a unit test asserting the helper's written y range for y0) would catch an origin mismatch. Each helper's footprint should be reported in the same coordinates as runParts' owned-cell table.

waste.what: Writing a view that drops writes below a height, so the chimney helper runs unchanged, meant hand-rolling a Proxy wrapper and checking which helper calls go through set/fill.
waste.cost: one Proxy wrapper of about 10 lines and one rebuild
waste.tool: runParts option { minY } / `view.above(y)` that clips a part's writes to the free band and reports what it dropped, so a part can be built in a locked shell without its own proxy.

companions.task: Take the shell's room air out of the four stack footprints (y0..17) and lay the chimney bricks through both floors, so the stacks stand solid through the rooms.
Set the firebox openings and campfire hearths in each stack face on both floors (y4..5 and y11..12) once the shell leaves those cells open, with the brick lintels and slab mantels.
Check the slate shed roof over the rear porch and the chimney flashing where the stacks come through the main hip, so the joins are watertight.

structured_output.summary:
Roofs and chimneys: the four brick stacks now build from y18 up through the roof with their signal fires, plus the rear-porch shed roof (448 placed).
REFUSED 224 -> 0 and OFF-PALETTE none; ./make.sh runs clean and writes build.nbt.
The in-house stack cells (grid y4..17) and the hearths are dropped, since the shell owns them.
left: Stacks inside the house are missing: the shell leaves air at the four stack footprints (x33-34/61-62, z46-47/56-57) from grid y3 to y17, so those cells are locked and this part can't write bricks there. Fix belongs in the shell: keep the stack columns solid (or exclude them from room air) for y0..17.
Stack bricks above the plate (y18 up) now float: nothing under them at y17, so the attic section is an unsupported group until the shell fix lands.

Hearths (fireboxes at y4..5 and y11..12 in each stack face) are not built. They were removed from roofs.mjs because every firebox write is in shell-owned cells; the firebox/hearth code needs to come back once the shell leaves those cells open.

Vocabulary offset, not fixed here (outside the two requested fixes): vocab/h4.mjs chimneyStack assumes grid y = site y + SITE_Y (4), but build.mjs and vocab/base.mjs use grid y = plan y. So chimneyStack(..., {y:0}) writes grid 4..31 instead of 0..27, and the stacks stand 4 cells too high. The one-line workaround is {y: -4} in roofs.mjs, or fix SITE_Y in h4.mjs.
The extra signal campfire at grid y27 (roofs.mjs) sits inside the stack under the chimneyStack flue; the owner of the chimney design should confirm it is wanted.

waste.what: Finding which cells were refused took several steps: the runParts report keeps only the first 8 refused writes (all at y4-5), so I had to re-run with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and tabulate the shell's owned cells by hand to learn the real set (16 columns x 14 rows, grid y4..17).
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one probe script; the 224-count was only explained after reading the lock code in build.mjs
waste.tool: runParts report should list every refused cell grouped by column or y-band (or write them to parts-report.json), not the first 8. A `mcd lock-map <part>` command that prints owned cells per part would show a footprint's conflicts in one table.

waste.what: Discovered that vocab/h4.mjs assumes a grid origin of site y -4 (SITE_Y = 4), contradicting vocab/base.mjs and build.mjs (grid y = plan y). Every helper using SITE_Y puts its stacks 4 cells high; I only found it by comparing the refused coordinates (grid y4) with the plan's y0.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls of reasoning from coordinates; nothing was built wrong beyond this part
waste.tool: A vocab conformance check (`mcd check --vocab`, or a unit test asserting the helper's written y range for y0) would catch an origin mismatch. Each helper's footprint should be reported in the same coordinates as runParts' owned-cell table.

waste.what: Writing a view that drops writes below a height, so the chimney helper runs unchanged, meant hand-rolling a Proxy wrapper and checking which helper calls go through set/fill.
waste.cost: one Proxy wrapper of about 10 lines and one rebuild
waste.tool: runParts option { minY } / `view.above(y)` that clips a part's writes to the free band and reports what it dropped, so a part can be built in a locked shell without its own proxy.

companions.task: Take the shell's room air out of the four stack footprints (y0..17) and lay the chimney bricks through both floors, so the stacks stand solid through the rooms.
Set the firebox openings and campfire hearths in each stack face on both floors (y4..5 and y11..12) once the shell leaves those cells open, with the brick lintels and slab mantels.
Check the slate shed roof over the rear porch and the chimney flashing where the stacks come through the main hip, so the joins are watertight.
